source.value: Given that $y=x^3+e^x$ for $x=x(t),$ and that $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ at the point where $x=1,$ find $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$

decisions.reason: Observed MA content supersedes the stored value

decisions.question: e-10899

source.question: e-10899
source.value:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={x}^{3}+{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}({x}^{3}+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3{x}^{2}+{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d y}{\textrm d t}=2$ and $x=1,$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d x}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3\cdot {1}^{2}+{e}^{1}) \\ 2 & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (3+e) \\ \frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{2}{3+e}.\end{aligned}
$$

decisions.question: e-10901

source.question: e-10901
source.value:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\dfrac{\textrm d r}{\textrm d t}=\sqrt{2}$ and $\theta=\dfrac{\pi}{4},$ and solve for $\dfrac{\textrm d \theta}{\textrm d t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡\theta  \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{4}) \\ \sqrt{2} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{2}}{2} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =\sqrt{2}\cdot \frac{2}{\sqrt{2}} \\ \frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t} & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

source.value:

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =x+{e}^{x} \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(x+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(x+{e}^{x}) \\ \frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\cdot (1+{e}^{x}).\end{aligned}
